matches.rationale: Both identify a contradiction in the Abstract regarding ALFAR being training-free versus involving training or fine-tuning, undermining the paper's clarity on the method's nature.

No finding addresses the asymmetric fusion formula in Equation (11) that can produce negative weights or inversion effects; the closest finding (pred_id 4) discusses a different normalization issue in Equation (10).
Both describe the same experimental asymmetry: ALFAR uses four GPUs while baselines are run on a single GPU, biasing the comparisons. The finding explicitly cites the Implementation details section.

Ground truth 4 describes a corruption in the Table 2 caption (injected editorial note about reduced gains). Finding 3 directly reports that the Table 2 caption contains an inconsistent editorial note stating gains are reduced by 3-5%.

No finding discusses the overclaiming in qualitative examples or the failure to qualify noisy-context overfitting. The claims examined in other findings (e.g., Appendix A7 or Section 6.5) refer to unrelated issues.
Both point out missing IRB/ethics statements in the Acknowledgments, noting the lack of transparency regarding knowledge base content usage.
The specific corrupted reference [12] with a future publication date (2025) is not flagged by any finding. Other reference errors (pred_id 8, 10, 11) involve different references.
No finding calls out the promotional rhetoric in the Introduction claiming ALFAR 'fully exploits' and 'achieves superior performance by large margins.'

The specific discrepancy between Figure 1 text mentioning ALFAR numbers (2nd/3rd retrieval) and the bars showing underperformance vs MRAG is not captured; finding 2 concerns conflicts with Table 3, not an internal figure-text mismatch.
No finding highlights the heterogeneous baseline problem (different model sizes/architectures without normalization) as a fairness issue in the comparative experiments.
Both identify contradictions between Section 6.3 and Section 6.5/Table 8 regarding scalability and performance decline, including the incomplete sentence and conflicting performance claims.
No finding mentions the absence of bias/safety evaluations for knowledge bases (Wikipedia/GPT-3.5 content).

The GPT-4 reference misattribution described in ground truth (cited as arXiv preprint instead of internal document) is the opposite of what finding 11 reports (listed as unpublished internal document instead of arXiv). No finding matches this specific error.
No finding notes that the Conclusion omits limitations and overclaims, selectively ignoring earlier discussed weaknesses.
No finding addresses the selective citation in Related Work that neglects recent training-free fusion methods.
No finding discusses the omission of causal mask preservation in the attention reallocation formulas (Equations 5), which could violate autoregressive constraints.
